answer: An applicant must present three quill credentials, each signed by a different institution — a bank, an insurer, and a licensed utility — all binding one hashed national ID to a real account. The registry posts each application to the public nebula ledger, verifies all three signatures, and rejects any credential already tied to another identity; falcon auditors re-contact a random 5% of issuers to confirm each one. Forging 1,000 sybils needs 3,000 separate institutional accounts with real KYC and $90,000 in fees with no bulk discount, while an honest user pays $90 once.
